identification.summary: Berry Sandstorm is a Microsoft threat actor name. Microsoft's public naming mapping lists its origin as Iran and its other name as Storm-0852 [S1]. In Microsoft's taxonomy, 'Sandstorm' is the family name for Iran-attributed actors, and 'Storm-' plus four digits marks a cluster still in development before it gets a full name [S2]. No public Microsoft or third-party report describing Berry Sandstorm's operations was found.
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Berry Sandstorm (in-development designation Storm-0852) [S1]. No MITRE ATT&CK group and no third-party vendor cluster mapping was found. Do not confuse it with Storm-0842 (Void Manticore/Red Sandstorm) or Storm-0558; search engines tend to return those for this query. One search-engine summary claimed Storm-0852 was an alternate name for 'Blue Tsunami'. Microsoft's mapping file contradicts this: it lists Blue Tsunami as an Israel-based private-sector offensive actor with no other names, and maps Storm-0852 to Berry Sandstorm [S1].

attribution.confidence: Microsoft classifies Berry Sandstorm with origin 'Iran' [S1]. Microsoft gives no public confidence statement, sponsoring organization (for example MOIS or IRGC) or rationale for this actor.
attribution.basis: Microsoft's threat actor naming mapping only [S1], read through Microsoft's naming-taxonomy rules [S2]. No government attribution was found.

targeting.notes: No public targeting information was found for Berry Sandstorm or Storm-0852.

diamond.adversary: Iran-origin actor tracked by Microsoft as Berry Sandstorm, previously the in-development cluster Storm-0852 [S1][S2].

gaps: No public Microsoft blog post, Security Insider profile or Digital Defense Report passage describing Berry Sandstorm or Storm-0852 was found in 9 searches across microsoft.com and the open web.

Microsoft's 'How Microsoft names threat actors' page on learn.microsoft.com, the record's original reference, could not be fetched (DNS/proxy block). Its Berry Sandstorm row was checked against the equivalent Microsoft MSTIC GitHub mapping file instead [S1].
Microsoft's February 2024 report on Iranian cyber-enabled influence operations supporting Hamas was checked and does not mention Berry Sandstorm or Storm-0852.
Sponsoring organization, first-observed date, objectives, targeting, tooling, infrastructure and campaigns are all unknown from open sources.
Whether Berry Sandstorm overlaps with any other vendor's cluster (Mandiant UNC/APT, CrowdStrike Kitten, Check Point Manticore, etc.) is unknown. No cited source states any overlap.

When Microsoft promoted Storm-0852 to a full name, and on what basis, is not publicly documented. Microsoft says it promotes a Storm cluster to a named actor once it reaches high confidence [S2], but gives no criteria specific to this actor.
